name: Boris Aronov
milestone_by_age_26: No material, independently verified career-defining milestone by age 26 found. BA (1984, age ~21) and MS (1986, age ~23) are standard academic steps; PhD under Micha Sharir at NYU Courant was completed in 1989 (age ~25–26) but without contemporaneous awards, breakthrough publications with public impact, or faculty appointment clearly dated ≤26 in reviewed sources.
early_history_summary: Born March 13, 1963. Earned a BA in computer science and mathematics from Queens College, CUNY (1984), then MS (1986) and PhD (1989) at NYU Courant under Micha Sharir in computational geometry. Later became a Sloan Research Fellow and a professor at NYU Tandon.
evidence_summary: Aronov followed a strong but standard research-training path (Queens College → Courant PhD). His recognized research career and Sloan Fellowship are later. Without a clearly dated exceptional milestone at or before age 26, he is coded ineligible under the strict age-26 rule.

name: Emily Best
milestone_by_age_26: Major milestones came after age 26: produced Like the Water around 2010 (age ~30) and publicly launched Seed&Spark in December 2012 (age ~32). No material dated milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born August 4, 1980 in California; raised in Sacramento. Studied anthropology and American studies at Haverford College and music in Barcelona. Worked as an actress and restaurant manager before producing film and founding Seed&Spark.
family_context_summary: Mother was a fiction writer who became a cable company executive; father a journalist turned strategy consultant.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents worked in media/writing and consulting; not a direct tech-startup domain apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Best’s breakout as Seed&Spark founder and film producer occurred in her early 30s. Education and early jobs do not constitute a material success-by-26 milestone under the rubric.

name: Greg Fitzgerald
milestone_by_age_26: No publicly documented birth year found for Solana co-founder/principal engineer Greg Fitzgerald. Solana Labs was founded around 2017–2018 after Qualcomm staff engineering work; without a confirmed birth year, a material milestone by age 26 cannot be established. (Wikipedia’s Greg Fitzgerald page is a different person—a UK housebuilding executive born 1964.)
early_history_summary: Fitzgerald is a technical co-founder of Solana who wrote much of the early Rust implementation. He previously worked at Qualcomm on systems software and is listed as co-founder/CTO/principal engineer of Solana Labs; education sources cite UIUC computer engineering and UCSD compiler study.
evidence_summary: Solana co-founding is a major technical achievement but occurred after multi-year Qualcomm tenure and cannot be age-verified without a birth year. Strict eligibility requires a dated ≤26 milestone.

name: Elena Silenok
milestone_by_age_26: No publicly documented birth year found. Clothia was founded around 2010–2012 after FAU undergrad, UCSD MS, and industry roles; without a confirmed birth year, a material milestone by age 26 cannot be established.
early_history_summary: Grew up in Russia near the Baltic Sea as an only child of mechanical engineers. At 15 won a US-government exchange scholarship to California; later BS at Florida Atlantic University and MS in network security at UCSD; worked at ATT, Abacus, and as a consultant before founding Clothia (virtual closet/AR try-on).
family_context_summary: Only child of two mechanical engineers in Russia; came to the US as a teen exchange student.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were mechanical engineers; technical household but not fashion-tech entrepreneurship.
evidence_summary: Silenok’s Clothia founding is the clearest career milestone but is undated relative to age without a birth year. She is currently described as a tech founder turned investor (Moneta Luna). Ineligible under strict age verification.

name: David J. Brown
milestone_by_age_26: In 1982, at about age 25, co-founded Silicon Graphics (SGI) as one of seven Stanford technical staff who joined Jim Clark to build the company that pioneered 3D graphics workstations.
early_history_summary: Educated at the University of Pennsylvania Moore School (BSE 1979, MSE 1980 under Ruzena Bajcsy). Joined Stanford Computer Science research staff in 1981 working on the SUN workstation with Andreas Bechtolsheim, then left with Clark’s group to form Silicon Graphics in 1982.
family_context_summary: Primary and secondary education in Delmar, New York; family financial and parental occupational details not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Brown moved from Penn’s Moore School into Stanford’s early-1980s systems research group around the SUN workstation, then co-founded Silicon Graphics at ~25 with Jim Clark and six other Stanford staff. That places him inside the densest hardware-startup ecosystem of the era with complementary technical peers. Family background is not documented; later career included DEC DECstation work, Sun/Solaris architecture, and ACM Queue founding editorship.
starting_point: Raised and schooled in Delmar, New York; family class and parental occupations not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Computer scientist known as SGI co-founder and longtime systems architect (Sun/Solaris, ACM Queue); living; public profile primarily historical/academic as of mid-2020s.

trajectory.event: Earned BSE from University of Pennsylvania Moore School of Electrical Engineering.
Joined Stanford CS research staff working on the SUN workstation project with Andreas Bechtolsheim.
Co-founded Silicon Graphics with Jim Clark and six other Stanford technical staff.
Matriculated at St John's College, Cambridge for doctoral work introducing Unified Memory Architecture ideas.
Joined Sun Microsystems and later defined the Solaris application binary interface and architecture processes.
Became a founding editor of ACM Queue magazine.

name: Matt Flannery
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Kiva in late 2004–2005 and left TiVo full-time for Kiva in December 2005 at about age 28 (Computerworld listed him as age 30 in July 2007; a profile states he started Kiva at 28). No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Stanford BS in Symbolic Systems and MA in philosophy. Worked as a programmer at TiVo while developing Kiva after filming microbusiness stories in East Africa for Village Enterprise Fund. Led Kiva as CEO through early growth, later co-founded Branch.co.
evidence_summary: Kiva is a landmark social-enterprise success, but founding and full-time commitment occurred around age 28, outside the ≤26 window. Birth year ~1977 inferred from age 30 in July 2007 Computerworld profile.

name: Robert Kahn
milestone_by_age_26: Completed Princeton PhD in electrical engineering in 1964 at age 25, but defining work (ARPANET design at BBN, TCP/IP with Cerf in the 1970s) occurred after age 30. No material career-defining milestone by age 26 beyond standard advanced degrees.
early_history_summary: Born December 23, 1938 in Brooklyn to Beatrice and Lawrence Kahn. BS electrical engineering CCNY (1960), MA (1962) and PhD (1964) from Princeton under Bede Liu. Later principal ARPANET architect at BBN and co-designer of TCP/IP; Turing Award 2004.
family_context_summary: Ashkenazi Jewish family in Brooklyn; father Lawrence Kahn; related through his father to futurist Herman Kahn.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as engineering/networking domain expertise transferred to Robert in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Kahn is a tier-1 Internet pioneer, but the rubric requires a material dated milestone ≤26. His PhD at 25 is academic completion; ARPANET and TCP/IP fame arrived in his 30s and later. Strict coding: age_26_ineligible.

name: Mike Little
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded WordPress with Matt Mullenweg in 2003 (first release May 27, 2003) at about age 40–41. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born May 12, 1962 in Manchester; Nigerian father (math lecturer/musician) and English mother (primary teacher); fostered then adopted; raised on a Stockport council estate. Web developer who forked b2/cafelog with Mullenweg into WordPress.
family_context_summary: Mixed Nigerian-English parentage; early foster care and adoption; working-class Stockport council-estate upbringing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father mathematics lecturer and musician; mother primary school teacher—education-oriented household, not web software.
evidence_summary: WordPress co-founding is historically huge but occurred when Little was about 41. No ≤26 material milestone is documented.

name: Mary Kenneth Keller
milestone_by_age_26: Entered the Sisters of Charity BVM in 1932 (age ~18) and took vows in 1940 (age ~26), but her defining CS milestones—BS 1943 (age ~29), MS 1953, PhD in computer science 1965 (age ~51), BASIC-related work, and founding Clarke College’s CS department—all occurred after age 26.
early_history_summary: Born Evelyn Marie Keller in Cleveland, December 17, 1913. Became Sister Mary Kenneth; earned math degrees at DePaul and the first US woman CS PhD (Wisconsin–Madison, 1965). Founded computer science at Clarke College and advocated computing in education.
family_context_summary: Daughter of John Adam Keller and Catherine Josephine Sullivan Keller of Cleveland; further family financial detail not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as computing-domain advantage in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Keller is a pioneering woman in computing, but her PhD and departmental founding came decades after age 26. Religious vocation by 26 is not a CS career milestone under this rubric.

name: Pavel Durov
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded and launched VKontakte (VK) for beta in September 2006 at age 21; the network scaled to 1 million users by July 2007 (age 22) and became Russia’s dominant social network.
early_history_summary: Born October 10, 1984 in Leningrad; spent much of childhood in Turin, Italy where father Valery Durov taught. Studied at Saint Petersburg State University (2002–2006), ran popular student forum spbgu.ru, then with classmates and brother Nikolai built VK as a Facebook-like Russian social network while still university-aged.
family_context_summary: Father Valery Durov is a Doctor of Philological Sciences and longtime head of classical philology at SPbU; mother from a Ukrainian family line (Ivanenko). Academic household; childhood years in Italy.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father is a classical philology professor—elite academic capital but not software entrepreneurship. Brother Nikolai is a multiple math/programming olympiad winner who became VK/Telegram technical co-architect.
evidence_summary: Durov launched VK at 21 with capital from classmate Mirilashvili and deep technical help from brother Nikolai, riding the global social-network wave after Facebook. Early student-forum building, university immersion, and a complementary founding team compounded quickly; family academic status provided modest safety but not a tech network. He later co-founded Telegram (2013), left Russia after conflict with authorities, and remains Telegram CEO with multi-billion-dollar status despite 2024 French legal proceedings.
starting_point: Born in Leningrad (1984) to an academic philology professor father; spent much of childhood in Turin, Italy; returned for university at Saint Petersburg State University.
current_position: CEO of Telegram; multi-billionaire founder (Forbes net worth fluctuates, ~$6–15B range in recent years); holds multiple citizenships; faced French charges in 2024 related to Telegram moderation, released under judicial supervision.

trajectory.event: Launched VKontakte in beta and registered the domain; became CEO of the new Russian social network.
VK reached 1 million users and was incorporated as a Russian private company.
VK overtook Odnoklassniki as Russia’s most popular social network.
Co-founded encrypted messaging app Telegram with brother Nikolai while still associated with VK.
Forced out as VK CEO after refusing FSB data requests; left Russia and focused on Telegram.
Telegram raised ~$1.7B toward TON/Gram crypto plans later blocked by the SEC.
Arrested in France on charges tied to Telegram content moderation and cooperation with authorities; released on bail under judicial supervision.

name: Ravindra K. Ahuja
milestone_by_age_26: Completed IIT Kanpur BS (1977), MS (1979), and PhD (1982, age ~26) and joined IIT Kanpur faculty—strong but standard elite-academic progression. Career-defining Lanchester Prize (1993), Optym founding (2000), and major practice awards came well after age 26.
early_history_summary: Born February 20, 1956 in Rampur, Uttar Pradesh. Full education at IIT Kanpur through PhD (1982) on parametric programming in network flows; later MIT visiting roles, University of Florida professor, and founder/CEO of Optym (Innovative Scheduling).
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond birthplace in Rampur, India.
evidence_summary: Ahuja is a highly decorated OR/network-optimization scholar-entrepreneur, but the ≤26 bar is not clearly cleared by exceptional non-standard milestones—PhD and home-institution faculty at ~26 are expected outcomes of the IIT pipeline rather than a breakout success event.

name: Forest Baskett
milestone_by_age_26: BA Rice 1965 (age ~22) and PhD University of Texas at Austin 1970 (age ~26–27; born May 11, 1943—PhD year likely at or after turning 27). Stanford professorship began 1971 (age ~27–28). Cray-1 OS work, BCMP networks paper (1975), SGI CTO, and NEA partnership all later. No clearly dated material milestone at age ≤26.
early_history_summary: Born May 11, 1943 in Texas. BA mathematics Rice (1965); PhD computer science UT Austin (1970) on multiprogrammed systems models. Stanford CS/EE professor 1971–1982 (advised Andy Bechtolsheim); later DEC Western Research Lab, SGI CTO/SVP R&D, and NEA general partner.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Texas; detailed family financial/occupational background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Baskett’s impactful systems career and VC career are well documented, but the first clearly dated senior milestones (Stanford faculty 1971, major papers mid-1970s) sit at or after age 27. Conservative coding marks him age_26_ineligible.
